name: Washer Drain Pump Amperage
purpose: Confirm drain pump motor draws expected current when commanded to run.
failureModes: Zero amps on drain call: open winding, failed motor, control/relay not energizing pump
High amps: pump jammed with debris, seized bearing/impeller
testingTips: Clamp meter on pump lead during an active drain call, not spin
Check for coin/debris jam in pump housing before condemning motor
notes: Small AC drain pump motors vary by brand/model — verify against nameplate when available

name: Washer Drain Pump Winding Resistance
purpose: Verify drain pump motor winding continuity to rule out open winding when pump doesn't run.
failureModes: Open (OL): failed motor winding
Very low reading: shorted winding, likely trips breaker/blows fuse when energized
testingTips: Disconnect power and unplug pump connector before testing
Wide range across brands — treat as a continuity/sanity check, not a tight spec
notes: Resistance varies significantly by pump design (AC shaded-pole vs. DC) — verify against manufacturer spec when known

name: Washer Water Inlet Valve Coil Resistance
purpose: Verify hot/cold water inlet valve solenoid coil continuity when a fill issue is present on one or both circuits.
failureModes: Open (OL): failed solenoid coil — no fill on that circuit even with good water pressure/supply
Very low reading: shorted coil
testingTips: Test each solenoid coil (hot/cold) separately at the valve connector
Rule out supply-side issues (screens, pressure, kinked hose) before condemning valve
notes: Coil resistance varies by valve design and flow rating — verify against manufacturer spec when known

name: Washer Door Lock/Switch Continuity
purpose: Verify door lock/switch contact closes (near-zero resistance) when door is closed and latched.
failureModes: Open (OL) with door closed: failed switch contact, misaligned striker, wiring fault
Closed (low ohms) with door open: switch stuck closed — safety concern, do not run unit until resolved
testingTips: Test at the connector with door manually held closed/latched
On front-load units with a PTC heater-style lock mechanism, this is contact continuity only — the PTC heating element itself is a separate, model-specific component
notes: Applies to simple switch-contact style locks; PTC/heater-style lock mechanisms need manufacturer override values

name: Washer Drive Motor Winding Resistance
purpose: Verify drive motor winding continuity when motor fails to run or trips on start.
failureModes: Open (OL) on any winding: failed motor
Very low reading between winding and frame/case: grounded winding
testingTips: Disconnect motor connector and power before testing
On PMDC/BLDC drive motors, phase-to-phase readings should be close to equal — large mismatch suggests a bad winding
notes: Resistance varies widely between belt-drive AC motors and direct-drive PMDC/BLDC motors — verify against manufacturer spec when known

name: Dishwasher Circulation Pump Amperage
purpose: Confirm circulation/wash pump motor draws expected current during wash cycle.
failureModes: Zero amps: open winding, failed motor, control not energizing pump
High amps: pump/impeller jammed, motor bearing failure
testingTips: Clamp on pump motor lead during active wash phase
Some models share one motor for wash and drain via a reversing or diverter mechanism — confirm design before isolating a fault
notes: Verify against motor nameplate rating — some models combine wash/drain functions on a single motor

name: Dishwasher Drain Pump Amperage
purpose: Confirm drain pump motor draws expected current when commanded to run (on models with a dedicated drain pump).
failureModes: Zero amps on drain call: open winding, failed motor, control not energizing pump
High amps: pump jammed with debris (food, glass, labels)
testingTips: Clamp meter on pump lead during an active drain call
Check air gap/check valve and drain hose routing before condemning pump on slow-drain complaints
notes: Not all models have a dedicated drain pump — some use a single reversible motor; verify design before applying

name: Dishwasher Water Inlet Valve Coil Resistance
purpose: Verify fill valve solenoid coil continuity when unit fails to fill or underfills.
failureModes: Open (OL): failed solenoid coil, no fill
Very low reading: shorted coil
testingTips: Test at valve connector with power disconnected
Rule out supply-side screen/pressure issues before condemning valve
notes: Coil resistance varies notably by brand/valve design — verify against manufacturer spec when known

name: Dishwasher Heating Element Resistance
purpose: Verify heating element continuity and resistance to rule out open or shorted element on no-heat/no-dry complaints.
failureModes: Open (OL): no heat for wash boost or dry cycle
Reading well outside range: shorted or damaged element
testingTips: Disconnect power before testing at element terminals
Use nameplate wattage with Ohm's law (R = V²/W) to sanity-check reading if spec unknown
notes: Verify model spec — wattage varies by tub size, typically 700-1100W on 120V

name: Dishwasher Door Latch Switch Continuity
purpose: Verify door latch switch contact closes when door is closed/latched, allowing cycle to start.
failureModes: Open (OL) with door latched: failed switch, misaligned latch
Closed with door open: switch stuck — safety concern
testingTips: Test at connector with door manually held closed/latched
Many models have two switches (start-enable and secondary safety) — test each separately

name: Magnetron Filament Resistance
purpose: Verify magnetron filament continuity when unit powers on but does not heat.
failureModes: Open (OL): failed magnetron filament — unit runs but produces no heat
Reading to chassis/case (should be OL): grounded magnetron, replace
testingTips: DISCONNECT POWER AND DISCHARGE THE HV CAPACITOR before any testing — HV circuit can hold a lethal charge even unplugged
Use lowest ohms range; filament reads very low, near meter's zero — a good filament often just barely registers above 0
Also check filament-to-case for a short (should read open/OL)
notes: Standard DMMs struggle to resolve sub-1Ω readings precisely — treat as continuity pass/fail more than a precise value

name: High-Voltage Capacitor Capacitance
purpose: Verify HV capacitor is near its rated capacitance; a degraded cap reduces HV output to the magnetron.
failureModes: Reading well below rating: degraded/failing capacitor, weak or no heat
Reading at 0/open: failed capacitor
testingTips: DISCONNECT POWER AND FULLY DISCHARGE THE CAPACITOR before touching leads — this component stores a dangerous, potentially lethal charge even with the unit unplugged
Use a capacitance meter rated for the component; a simple ohmmeter charge/discharge kick only confirms rough function, not capacitance value
notes: Common rated value is ~1.0 µF at ~2100V but this varies by model/wattage — treat as manufacturer override needed for exact spec

name: High-Voltage Diode Check
purpose: Confirm HV diode blocks in one direction and does not read a short in either direction.
failureModes: Reads low/near-zero in both directions: shorted diode — will damage magnetron/transformer if not replaced
Reads open (OL) in both directions: open diode — no rectification, no or weak heat
testingTips: DISCONNECT POWER AND FULLY DISCHARGE THE HV CAPACITOR before testing — this circuit can be lethal even unplugged
Standard ohmmeters use a low test voltage and are not fully reliable on HV diodes rated for kV-range blocking — a diode-mode reading is a rough sanity check only, not a definitive pass
When in doubt, replace as a low-cost part rather than relying solely on an ohmmeter verdict
notes: No standard normal/typical numeric range applies — this is a directional short/open check, not a value comparison; manufacturer test procedure should be followed when available

name: Microwave Door Interlock Switch Continuity
purpose: Verify each door interlock switch (primary, secondary/interlock, monitor) operates correctly for safe HV operation.
failureModes: Primary/secondary open when door closed: unit won't start
Monitor switch stuck closed with door open: may blow the fuse by design (safety fail-safe) — do not defeat or bypass
testingTips: Disconnect power before testing at connector
Test each switch individually — most units have 2-3 interlock switches with distinct functions, not interchangeable
Never bypass interlock switches for testing purposes; they are a safety system

name: Gas Valve Safety Coil Resistance
purpose: Verify gas valve solenoid coil continuity when valve fails to open on ignition call.
failureModes: Open (OL): failed coil — valve will not open even with correct voltage present
Very low reading: shorted coil
testingTips: Disconnect power before testing at valve coil terminals
Confirm the valve is actually receiving voltage from the control board/igniter circuit before condemning the coil
notes: Coil resistance varies by valve manufacturer and design — verify against manufacturer spec when known

name: Hot Surface Igniter Resistance
purpose: Verify igniter continuity and rough resistance when igniter fails to glow or gas doesn't ignite.
failureModes: Open (OL): failed igniter, most common no-ignition cause
Igniter glows but gas doesn't light: igniter may be too weak to trip the safety valve current draw — check amp draw, not just resistance
testingTips: Disconnect power before checking resistance at igniter terminals
Silicon carbide igniters read noticeably different (generally higher cold resistance) than silicon nitride igniters — do not treat these as interchangeable specs
For a running verification, an amp-draw test (typically ~3.0-3.6A for silicon carbide type) is often more diagnostic than a static cold-resistance reading
notes: Silicon carbide vs. silicon nitride igniters have meaningfully different normal ranges — verify igniter type and manufacturer spec before relying on this value
